stories.title: Dov Hertz Offloads Major Staten Island Industrial Site for $167M
stories.excerpt: A 53-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) parcel on Staten Island just changed hands for $167 million. Real estate investment firm Jadian Capital acquired the property at 1900 and 1800 South Avenue, located on the island’s west shore, from Dov Hertz’s Kadima Industrial Partners, according to broker Cushman & Wakefield. The Real Deal first reported the news. “A well-deserved congrats to Kadima Industrial Partners and our buyer for closing one of the market’s largest industrial outdoor storage trades,” Kyle Schmidt, a vice chairman at C&W, wrote in a LinkedIn post Tuesday. “Fully leased, the 53-acre property illustrates the continued user and capital demand for sites offering proximity to infrastructure and consumers.” Spokespeople for C&W, Jadian Capital and Kadima Industrial did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. Schmidt listed C&W brokers Gary Gabriel, Ryan Larkin, Seth Zuidema, Helen McCarthy Paul, Rico Murtha and Gurpreet Singh in his LinkedIn post as representing the seller. It is unclear who represented the buyer in this deal. Hertz’s DH Property Holdings had acquired both Staten Island sites in two separate transactions — one in 2020 and the other in 2021 — for a total of $79 million, according to TRD. Since then, the property owner spent about $10 million in capital projects on the site. The property is fully leased to asphalt mixing plant City Asphalt and auction house IAA, with both a waterfront dock and train access. Jadian will continue to operate the property as an IOS facility, according to TRD. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Jadian Capital acquired 53-acre industrial outdoor storage site, Staten Island, $167M.
Fully leased property reflects continued user and capital demand for logistics-adjacent real estate.
West Shore Staten Island location offers proximity to port infrastructure and consumer markets.
stories.summary: Kadima Industrial Partners sold a fully leased 53-acre industrial outdoor storage parcel at 1900 and 1800 South Avenue on Staten Island's west shore to Jadian Capital for $167 million. The deal underscores strong investor appetite for last-mile and logistics-adjacent properties with existing cash flow and infrastructure proximity. The property's lease-up and rapid capital deployment signal sustained investor confidence in industrial assets tied to consumer goods distribution.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. However, the deal reflects ongoing investor capital rotation toward industrial and logistics assets, which may divert institutional capital flows and debt capacity away from multifamily underwriting in the Tri-State region. The premium pricing on leased industrial assets may also elevate land and construction cost expectations across competing property types in Staten Island and Brooklyn submarkets.

stories.title: Lincoln Property Partnership Acquires $450M Mixed-Use Tri-State Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower and Waterfall Asset Management have acquired a $450-million Tri-State portfolio spanning four million square feet of existing properties and prime development sites across 300 acres in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut. The portfolio is headlined by iPark 84 in East Fishkill, NY, a 270-acre business park comprising approximately 1.8 million square feet originally built for IBM’s flagship semiconductor manufacturing plant. The campus can accommodate more than 1.5 million square feet of additional development and is well positioned with existing infrastructure and immediately available power capacity. Additional assets include Edgewater Harbor, in Edgewater, NJ a 262-unit waterfront mixed-use community on the Hudson River; 761 Main Avenue in Norwalk, CT, an approximately 400,000-square-foot mixed-use center featuring a Northwell Health anchored medical outpatient complex, Cannondale bicycles headquarters, a 70,0000-square-foot Club Studio gym, and pads for entitled multifamily developments; and Trilogy Lofts in Yonkers, NY, a newly developed transit-oriented multifamily community adjacent to the Tuckahoe Metro-North station. “This acquisition is a milestone in Lincoln’s rapid growth across the Tri-State region,” said Jared Toothman, EVP and Market Leader at Lincoln. “The portfolio complements Lincoln’s robust national industrial, healthcare, and retail platforms as well as our multifamily development pipeline of over 5,000 units in the New York metro area.” The post Lincoln Property Partnership Acquires $450M Mixed-Use Tri-State Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lincoln Property/Saber-Hightower/Waterfall acquired $450M Tri-State portfolio: 4M sf across NY, NJ, CT.
Portfolio includes 270-acre iPark 84 (East Fishkill, NY) with 1.5M sf development capacity.
Key assets: 262-unit waterfront mixed-use (Edgewater, NJ), 400K sf mixed-use Norwalk (CT), transit-oriented Trilogy Lofts (Yonkers, NY).
stories.summary: Lincoln Property Company, Saber-Hightower, and Waterfall Asset Management acquired a $450 million mixed-use portfolio across the Tri-State region spanning 4 million square feet and 300 acres. Major holdings include iPark 84 (a 270-acre former IBM semiconductor campus with 1.5 million square feet of untapped development potential), Edgewater Harbor (262-unit waterfront community in Edgewater, NJ), and Trilogy Lofts (new transit-oriented multifamily in Yonkers near Metro-North). The deal signals aggressive capital redeployment into Tri-State assets with mixed-use and development optionality.
stories.impact: Signals institutional conviction in Tri-State multifamily-plus-mixed-use development. The iPark 84 acquisition with 1.5M sf remaining capacity and immediate power infrastructure suggests a long-term build-to-suit or conversion strategy; this could signal rising demand for suburban office-to-residential conversion in East Fishkill and surrounding Hudson Valley markets. Metro-North-anchored assets (Trilogy Lofts, Yonkers positioning) indicate capital targeting transit-dependent demand, heightening competition for development sites along Yonkers-Westchester corridors. Large institutional capital entry may push land and hard costs upward for competing developers in these submarkets.

stories.title: Jaime Lee Joins Kennedy Wilson After Two Decades at L.A. Powerhouse Jamison
stories.excerpt: After recently stepping down as the head of her family’s real estate firm — one of the most active developers in Los Angeles — Jaime Lee is taking a new role at Kennedy Wilson as senior managing director of capital markets and investments. Kennedy Wilson has approximately $37 billion in assets under management across equity, credit and development strategies in the United States and Europe. The Beverly Hills-based investment management firm announced on Wednesday that it hired Lee. Lee will help lead capital formation, strengthen relationships with institutional investors and strategic partners, and pursue investments across the company’s global platform, the announcement said. The move follows more than two decades for Lee at Jamison, most recently as CEO, where she helped grow the family-run company’s portfolio to roughly 18 million square feet spanning office, multifamily, retail and medical properties, while establishing Jamison as one of Los Angeles’ most prolific office-to-residential developers. The move to Kennedy Wilson also comes less than two months after the firm partnered with Jamison on a major joint venture targeting 4,000 affordable units across the city, beginning with the conversion of Downtown L.A.’s former World Trade Center into 512 apartments. For her role at Jamison, Lee was regularly honored on Commercial Observer’s Power SoCal list, last year noting that Jamison had completed seven adaptive reuse projects since 2013, with three more under construction and another 10 in its pipeline at the time. At Kennedy Wilson, Lee is similarly bullish on multifamily. “As investors evaluate where to allocate capital in this next cycle, there is a particularly compelling opportunity in multifamily, where constrained supply and durable housing demand are creating attractive long-term fundamentals,” Lee said in a statement. Lee also serves on the executive committee for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic and Paralympic Games and as a California Coastal commissioner
bullets: Jaime Lee, ex-CEO Jamison, hired as Senior Managing Director of Capital Markets, Kennedy Wilson.
Jamison portfolio: ~18M sf; major LA office-to-residential developer and L.A. market powerhouse.
Move signals Jamison's potential portfolio shift; Kennedy Wilson asset base: $37B AUM across US and Europe.
stories.summary: Jaime Lee, former CEO of Jamison (a major Los Angeles family-owned developer with approximately 18 million square feet of mixed-use properties), joined Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director of Capital Markets and Investments. Lee will lead capital formation and pursue investments across Kennedy Wilson's $37 billion global platform. The move follows a recent Jamison-Kennedy Wilson joint venture targeting 4,000 units.
stories.impact: Significant indicator of capital and strategic realignment in Los Angeles multifamily development. Lee's departure from Jamison's day-to-day operations, combined with her role at Kennedy Wilson (a major institutional investor), suggests potential acceleration of Jamison asset monetization and portfolio rationalization. This likely signals an intention to recycle capital into new development or institutional partnerships, possibly indicating reduced Jamison greenfield development activity in favor of joint ventures or asset sales. For competing LA developers, this signals elevated institutional capital competition and potential pace of deal flow in the office-to-residential conversion space where Jamison has dominated.

stories.title: Massachusetts AG Orders Post-Merger Sale of Two Boston Apartment Towers
stories.excerpt: Two Boston apartment towers in the portfolio of newly merged Vivmark Residential will be sold under an agreement between Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Joy Campbell and the merger partners, Equity Residential and AvalonBay Communities. The agreement to sell the two-building Emerson Place is intended to ensure that the merger will not substantially reduce competition in the mid-rise and high-rise multifamily rental housing market in downtown Boston, Campbell’s office said. “When real estate companies consolidate market share, it can lead to higher prices, lower-quality amenities and worse lease terms for renters. This agreement protects Boston renters and ensures this merger doesn’t create unlawful market control,” said Campbell. The AG’s office will need to approve the would-be buyer for Emerson Place. In addition, Equity Residential and AvalonBay have agreed to make a $500,000 contribution to support affordable housing preservation and development in Quincy, where they collectively own and operate six apartment buildings. The post Massachusetts AG Orders Post-Merger Sale of Two Boston Apartment Towers appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Massachusetts AG orders Equity Residential/AvalonBay divestiture of Emerson Place, Boston (2-building tower).
Merger condition: preserve downtown Boston mid-rise/high-rise rental competition to prevent rent increases.
AvalonBay/EQR also committed $500K to affordable housing preservation in Quincy (6 buildings collectively owned).
stories.summary: Following their merger, Vivmark Residential (formed by Equity Residential and AvalonBay Communities) agreed to sell the two-building Emerson Place apartment complex in downtown Boston under Massachusetts Attorney General oversight. The divestiture is required to prevent substantial reduction in mid-rise and high-rise rental housing competition and consequent rent increases in downtown Boston. The merging parties also pledged $500,000 toward affordable housing in Quincy, where they collectively own six properties.
stories.impact: Highlights regulatory risk and competitive concentration scrutiny in major multifamily markets, particularly Boston. The AG's power to veto buyer approval and mandate portfolio divestitures creates deal execution risk and potential extended holding periods for non-core assets. For multifamily developers, this signals that further large-scale acquisitions or mergers in Boston's downtown core may face regulatory friction; conversely, it opens acquisition opportunities for non-Equity/AvalonBay developers to acquire Emerson Place at a potentially favorable valuation given forced-sale dynamics and regulatory timeline pressure. The precedent raises the bar for future Tri-State consolidation deals.

stories.title: Goldie Initiative Draws Record Applicant Pool for 45 Scholar Spots
stories.excerpt: The Goldie B. Wolfe Miller Women Leaders in Real Estate Initiative (The Goldie Initiative) recently announced scholarship winners for the upcoming school year. Since 2007, The Goldie Initiative has created a professional community of over 250 women with academic and leadership potential, known as Goldie Scholars. The Goldie Initiative received a record-breaking 145 applications, a 51% increase over the previous year, making the 2026-2027 selection cycle the most competitive in the program’s history. 34 new Goldie Scholars were selected for the upcoming academic year. Together with 11 returning scholars, the program will support a total cohort of 45 women pursuing graduate degrees relevant to commercial real estate. In addition to welcoming this new cohort, Goldie Gala Chicago will celebrate this year’s Shero award winner: Lisa Konieczka, Executive Vice President at CBRE Chicago.“The Goldie Initiative continues to elevate and empower the next generation of women in real estate, and this cohort is a powerful example of that mission in action,” said Julie Thick, 2026 Board President. The post Goldie Initiative Draws Record Applicant Pool for 45 Scholar Spots appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Goldie Initiative received 145 scholarship applications, 51% increase year-over-year.
Program supports 45 women scholars pursuing CRE-related graduate degrees.
Record applicant pool signals growing pipeline of women entering real estate development and capital roles.
stories.summary: The Goldie B. Wolfe Miller Women Leaders in Real Estate Initiative announced record demand for its 2026–2027 scholarship cycle, with 145 applications representing a 51% year-over-year increase. The program will support 45 women (34 new and 11 returning) pursuing graduate degrees in commercial real estate. The program has developed a professional community of over 250 women since 2007.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development markets or underwriting. However, the record applicant surge reflects strong talent pipeline growth in CRE, suggesting future ease in recruiting development, asset management, and capital roles—potentially reducing competitive hiring pressure on development teams. The trend may also signal heightened institutional focus on diversity hiring across major REITs and developers, indirectly affecting organizational culture and talent retention strategies.

stories.title: Rexford to Sell $1.2B SoCal Portfolio to EQT
stories.excerpt: Rexford Industrial Realty is significantly slimming down its portfolio in Southern California. The Los Angeles-based industrial real estate investment trust (REIT) announced it has agreed to sell a portfolio of properties to an affiliate of EQT Real Estate for approximately $1.2 billion. The deal is expected to close by the end of the third quarter. The sale is part of Rexford’s plan to unload $1.5 billion to $2 billion in non-core properties, and improve its portfolio and balance sheet. Rexford did not disclose the properties included in the portfolio, but said more details will be provided when the transaction closes. The assets were described as having limited long-term growth potential, greater competing supply, shorter remaining lease terms or above-market rents. The portfolio sold to EQT is expected to generate a 5.5 percent cash net operating income yield in 2027 due to anticipated move-outs and the drops to what are now above-market rents. “By strategically recycling capital from select non-core assets, we are concentrating our portfolio around the properties we believe offer the strongest long-term cash flow growth and value creation opportunity,” Rexford CEO Laura Clark said in a statement. Rexford plans to use the proceeds to pay down debt maturing in 2027, potentially repurchase shares under its $1 billion buyback program, and fund its redevelopment and development pipeline. Including the EQT deal, Rexford has now closed or has under contract about $1.5 billion of dispositions this year, and is in negotiations on more properties for sale. As of June 30, Rexford owned 409 properties encompassing approximately 49.9 million rentable square feet, all concentrated in infill Southern California. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Rexford Industrial selling ~$1.2B SoCal portfolio to EQT Real Estate; part of $1.5–2B non-core divestiture.
Divested assets: limited long-term growth, above-market rents, shorter lease terms, competing supply.
EQT portfolio expected to generate 5.5% NOI yield in 2027 post-move-out and rent normalization.
stories.summary: Rexford Industrial Realty agreed to sell approximately $1.2 billion of Southern California industrial properties to an EQT Real Estate affiliate, with closing expected by Q3. The sale is part of a broader $1.5–2 billion non-core asset divestiture aimed at improving Rexford's portfolio and balance sheet. The sold assets are characterized by limited long-term growth potential, above-market rents, and greater competing supply; EQT expects a 5.5% 2027 NOI yield after anticipated move-outs and rent normalization.
stories.impact: Signals capital rotation away from transitional and lease-roll industrial in Southern California, likely due to overbuilding and above-market rents that will compress yields. For multifamily developers, this indicates potential softening in LA industrial valuations and market rents, which may reduce land assembly competition and carried-land costs in industrial-adjacent submarkets (e.g., Commerce, Vernon, East LA). However, it also signals institutional capital (EQT) is acquiring SoCal industrial at 5.5% yields, which may pressure multifamily cap rates in the region if capital flows shift to value-add repositioning opportunities.

stories.title: Entre Commercial Realty Negotiates Long-Term Lease at Truck Maintenance Facility
stories.excerpt: Entre Commercial Realty executed the lease of a 16,932-square-foot industrial building located at 675 Greenleaf Avenue in Elk Grove Village, Illinois. Entre represented Nearby Truck Repair LLC, a local diesel mechanic and fleet repair operator. 675 Greenleaf is fully equipped for heavy-duty truck repair & features a fully secured 1.3-acre lot. Secured yard space of this scale is increasingly scarce across Chicago’s industrial corridors, and it was the decisive factor that brought Nearby Truck Repair to the table, giving the company a protected environment to store trucks, trailers, and equipment. Ian Pattison of Entre Commercial Realty and Brad Bullington of GC Realty & Development were the sole brokers in the transaction, and worked with local landlord Gullo International Development Corp. Register now: www.connectindustrialwest2026.com The post Entre Commercial Realty Negotiates Long-Term Lease at Truck Maintenance Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Entre Commercial leased 16,932-sf truck maintenance facility, 675 Greenleaf, Elk Grove Village, Illinois.
Nearby Truck Repair LLC tenant; 1.3-acre secured yard critical differentiator in tight Chicago industrial market.
Scarcity of large secured yard space across Chicago industrial corridors driving lease demand.
stories.summary: Entre Commercial Realty negotiated a long-term lease for a 16,932-square-foot heavy-duty truck repair facility at 675 Greenleaf Avenue in Elk Grove Village for Nearby Truck Repair LLC. The 1.3-acre secured yard was the decisive draw for the tenant, as large secured storage yards are increasingly scarce across Chicago's industrial corridors. The transaction reflects growing operational demand for specialized industrial space with outdoor storage capacity.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, highlights tight industrial supply in Chicago's West Valley (Elk Grove Village, Addison) submarkets, which may elevate land and construction costs for mixed-use or industrial-adjacent development. The tenant demand for secured yard space suggests niche industrial asset value, potentially raising acquisition prices for land with outdoor storage potential and limiting multifamily ground-up development opportunities in these corridors.

stories.title: Net-Leased Dutch Bros Property in Indiana Changes Hands
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap brokered the sale of a brand-new, net-leased Dutch Bros property in Valparaiso, Indiana. The property sold for $3.12 million. The 2,495-square-foot Dutch Bros property is located at 2510 Laporte Avenue as a Target outlot within Valparaiso Market Place. It operates under a new 15-year absolute triple-net lease and is corporately guaranteed by Boersma Bros, LLC. The property is surrounded by shopping destinations and is approximately one mile from the Valparaiso University campus.“This offering generated significant interest from investors, resulting in multiple competitive offers,” said Austin Weisenbeck, senior managing director investments. “Ultimately, we secured an Indiana-based buyer and closed the transaction at more than 96% of the listing price, demonstrating continued demand for high-quality net-leased assets in strong retail corridors.” Weisenbeck, Sean Sharko, Adrian Mendoza and Phoebe Klein, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s Chicago Oak Brook office, in association with Julia Evinger, Marcus & Millichap’s Indiana broker of record, marketed the property on behalf of the seller, a Midwest developer. The post Net-Leased Dutch Bros Property in Indiana Changes Hands appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap brokered sale of new Dutch Bros property, Valparaiso, Indiana, $3.12M.
2,495-sf property; 15-year absolute triple-net lease, corporately guaranteed.
Location: Target outlot in Valparaiso Market Place; ~1 mile from Valparaiso University campus.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap sold a brand-new Dutch Bros coffee property in Valparaiso, Indiana for $3.12 million. The 2,495-square-foot space operates under a new 15-year absolute triple-net lease with corporate guarantee from Boersma Bros, LLC and is located within Valparaiso Market Place, approximately one mile from Valparaiso University. The sale generated multiple competitive offers.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. The transaction reflects sustained investor interest in net-leased quick-service restaurant properties near college campuses and retail anchors, signaling stable demand for consumer-facing retail in mid-sized Midwest markets. For multifamily developers, proximity to Valparaiso University suggests a collegiate-oriented housing submarket; the competition for retail space may elevate ground-floor lease rates in any new mixed-use or student housing development near campus.

stories.title: Household Goods Seller Diamond Home Signs 7K-SF Lease at 20 West 36th Street
stories.excerpt: A household goods importer and distributor has signed a new office lease in Midtown South, Commercial Observer has learned. Diamond Home signed a 7,272-square-foot deal for the entire fifth floor of the Rosen family’s 20 West 36th Street with a term of ​​seven years and seven months in a relocation from 28 West 36th Street, according to the brokers. Asking rent for the building between Fifth Avenue and Avenue of the Americas was $46 per square foot, according to the landlord. Joel Kubie and Michael Beyda of Benchmark Properties negotiated on behalf of the tenant, while Max Koeppel of Koeppel Rosen, the leasing and management agent for the Rosen family portfolio, represented the landlord in-house. “This was the second deal in a short period of time that Koeppel Rosen and I have done,” Kubie said in a statement. Kubie and Beyda recently represented Expanscience, which took about 11,500 square feet at 39 West 19th Street. “Both Diamond Home and Expanscience are currently mid-renovation for their space with move-in dates in the next few months,” Kubie added. Other tenants in the 12-story property at 20 West 36th Street include security services firm Unity Building Security, which signed a lease for 3,439 square feet in November 2025, and educational development organization Publicolor, which renewed its 6,850 square feet in June 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Diamond Home signed 7,272-sf office lease, fifth floor, 20 West 36th Street, Midtown South; 7.5-year term.
Asking rent: $46/sf; relocated from 28 West 36th Street (same block).
Tenant currently mid-renovation; Rosen family portfolio asset managed by Koeppel Rosen.
stories.summary: Diamond Home, a household goods importer and distributor, leased the entire fifth floor of 20 West 36th Street in Midtown South for 7,272 square feet at $46 per square foot for a 7-year, 7-month term. The company relocated from nearby 28 West 36th Street and is currently undergoing space renovation. Benchmark Properties and Koeppel Rosen negotiated the deal on behalf of tenant and landlord (Rosen family portfolio), respectively.
stories.impact: Limited multifamily relevance. The transaction reflects modest Manhattan office leasing activity in Midtown South at $46/sf, consistent with broader office market softness. Importantly, the Rosen family portfolio (historically residential-focused in NYC) continues active office leasing and asset management, signaling potential office-to-residential conversion strategy over the medium term. For multifamily developers tracking Rosen portfolio intentions, watch for similar lease-backs or divestiture announcements in this corridor, which could signal upcoming residential redevelopment opportunities.

stories.title: Zar Property Buys NoHo’s 31-35 Great Jones Street for $21M
stories.excerpt: Zar Property NY has bought two NoHo mixed-use buildings at 31-35 Great Jones Street for $21 million, Commercial Observer has learned. The nearly identical adjacent buildings between Lafayette Street and the Bowery have been owned by the Scott family of Great Jones St. Realty for the last five decades, at least. The family is selling at a time when office, retail and residential have become more competitive in the area. “Great Jones Street is a special block with a character and cachet that is difficult to find anywhere else,” Dario Zar said in a statement. “This acquisition aligns closely with our recent purchases and checks the key boxes we look for in a property. The loft-style spaces, high ceilings and flexible layouts give us the opportunity to create upscale, efficient offices for today’s tenants.” Albert Sultan and Joseph Kassin of Kassin Sabbagh Realty, known simply as KSR, represented the seller in the transaction. The two commercial properties — one seven-story property and an adjacent three-story, late-19th-century building — were only on the market for about two months with competing offers until the sellers settled on a cash offer from Zar, according to Sultan. “With all the AI and tech tenants that are propping up the market in terms of leasing, the companies want to be centered around Downtown and live-work-play submarkets like SoHo and NoHo,” Sultan told CO. “I think that is a testament to why this building had as much interest; we had three or four buyers all competing for this.” But Zar did not waste any time, closing the deal within 30 days. Current tenants at the NoHo properties include art gallery Aicon Contemporary. Just across the street at 375 Lafayette Street, Minskoff Equities and Edison Properties are constructing two 99-unit multifamily properties where a parking lot currently sits. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Zar Property acquired 31-35 Great Jones Street, NoHo, for $21M; two buildings (7-story + 3-story).
Property held by Scott family for ~50 years; loft-style with high ceilings, flexible layouts.
Zar plans upscale office conversions; aligns with recent Zar acquisitions in NoHo area.
stories.summary: Zar Property NY acquired two adjacent mixed-use buildings at 31-35 Great Jones Street in NoHo for $21 million from the Scott family of Great Jones St. Realty, who had held the properties for approximately five decades. The nearly identical buildings feature loft-style spaces with high ceilings and flexible layouts. Zar intends to create upscale, efficient office spaces and views the acquisition as aligned with recent portfolio additions and its NoHo acquisition strategy.
stories.impact: Signals consolidation of NoHo mixed-use redevelopment opportunity by Zar Property, a developer focused on office-to-residential and mixed-use conversion. The $21M acquisition price for two aging loft buildings indicates Zar's conviction in NoHo rental demand and office conversion feasibility. For competing multifamily developers, this suggests rising acquisition prices for NoHo's remaining unconverted loft assets and potential acceleration of office-to-residential conversion competition in this submarket. The deal also indicates that family-held, long-term NoHo properties are finally monetizing, potentially opening a narrow window for alternative bidders before core NoHo assets enter institutional hands.
